problem: LLM-based ObjectNav methods suffer from high inference cost that blocks real-time decision making, and from a domain gap between the LLM's general knowledge and the specific demands of navigation scenarios.
motivation: LLMs offer strong common-sense reasoning and planning for ObjectNav, but querying them at every step is too slow and general knowledge is not tailored to indoor navigation. The paper takes inspiration from human dual-process cognition (fast intuition, slow deliberation) to call the LLM only when needed, and injects navigation-specific knowledge.
key_idea: Use a lightweight intuition module to decide when to invoke the LLM (Intuitive-Deliberate mechanism), and enhance the LLM with a hierarchical Scene Description Tree and a Navigation Example database for in-context learning.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The claim is that selective LLM invocation reduces computational overhead while structured scene descriptions and retrieved examples close the domain gap, improving both success and decision efficiency.
method: Intuition module: lightweight module that decides when to strategically invoke the LLM, reducing LLM calls.
Deliberate LLM reasoning: LLM performs high-level decision making when invoked, mimicking slow deliberate cognition.
Scene Description Tree: hierarchical description of spatial and semantic relationships of indoor environments supplied to the LLM.
Navigation Example database: stored navigation examples used for in-context learning to adapt the LLM to navigation.
